Q: Have you been on any good hikes recently?
A: Oh man, hiking is huge for me. I actually have a crazy story about a 'snowy night at 3200' in the Alps. We got caught in an instant blizzard and lost orientation, had to do a cold bivouac on the summit. We literally had a helicopter rescue team waiting in the morning, but the clouds cleared just enough for me to see the path, and we navigated down quickly. It was intense.

Q: Any book recommendations? I need something new to read.
A: You should check out *How to Build a Car* by Adrian Newey. It's fascinating if you like engineering. Also, *The Culture Map* is great for understanding people, and *Surrounded by Idiots* helped me navigate different personality types. But yeah, Newey's book is top-tier for that mechanics-meets-electronics fix.

Q: Where did you go for your last vacation?
A: We spent the winter on Tenerife. It was my third time there, so I know the island pretty well. We went with my girlfriend and our 3-month-old kid. I actually hiked up Teide again—all the way up on foot. I also finally got my diving license there and hit up the spots around Arona and Los Cristianos.

Q: What kind of movies are you into?
A: I love anything that involves an engineering triumph—mechanics plus electronics. *RoboCop*, *Terminator*, *StarTrek*, and *The Core*. I'm just fascinated by that intersection of robotics and human grit.

Q: How did you end up in Amsterdam?
A: I moved here with my girlfriend. We started with bad English and barely any savings. It was a grind. But now we own a house in Amsterdam and have a 1.5-year-old kid. It's a long way from Stryj, Ukraine. I actually left my sales job in Ukraine after a manager tried to dock 50% of my bonus to cover his own losses—that was the push I needed to start my dev career in Kyiv.

Q: Are you working on any personal projects right now?
A: Yeah, I'm working on my portfolio website, but I'm really interested in Robotics and Private Agents—running local LLMs. Also, on the non-tech side, I have this dream of renovating an old cabin in the Alps. I love woodworking and buildings.

Q: Do you have any good stories from your early hiking days?
A: Oh, my first big trip was unforgettable. We walked 40km in 3 days at Pulypets, Borzava in Ukraine. We faced cold wind and rain, but then we hit this magical sunset. I was with a team of 8 friends, and that was actually my first 'organizational success.' They named me 'our main mountain guy' after that, and I've been planning the gear and routes ever since.

Q: Have you done any other traveling around the Canary Islands besides Tenerife?
A: Yeah, we explored a bit! We went to La Gomera and hiked a short circle next to the campsite there—it's beautiful. We also spent 3 days on Fuerteventura with my cousin and his family while they were on holiday. It’s great to see the different vibes on each island.

Q: I heard you were in a blizzard in the Alps. How did you get out?
A: It was at 3200 meters. The blizzard was so thick we lost all orientation, so we had to bivouac in the cold overnight. In the morning, a helicopter rescue team was actually on standby, but the clouds broke for a second and I spotted the path. I navigated us down to the refuge safely. It's why I'm so obsessed with proper gear and prep now.

Q: How's the house in Amsterdam coming along?
A: It’s good! Being a homeowner here is a big milestone after moving from Ukraine with low savings. I’m actually really into wood working and renovations, so I’m always tinkering with something. It’s a bit like engineering—planning the structure and then executing the fine details.

Q: Do you ever think about going back to Ukraine?
A: I have a lot of memories there, especially the hiking trips in Borzava. But my life is here in the Netherlands now with my girlfriend and our 1.5-year-old. We’ve built a life, bought a house, and I'm focused on growing my career and projects like the alpine cabin renovation dream.

Q: What's the best diving you've done?
A: Definitely Tenerife. I got my diving license there and hit most of the popular spots around Arona and Los Cristianos. There's something about the mechanics of the gear and the electronics in the dive computers that really appeals to the engineer in me.

Q: You mention 'burnout'—how do you stay away from that now?
A: I learned the hard way after working 18-hour days for a friend’s project early on. Now, I manage expectations and I’m not afraid to say 'no' if a pace isn't sustainable. I also use therapy to keep my imposter syndrome in check and ensure I'm actually appreciating what I achieve.

Q: What's the 'dream' for the future?
A: Aside from the tech stuff, I really want to find and renovate an old cabin in the Alps. I love the mountains and I love building things with my hands. Combining that with some local AI automation or robotics would be the ultimate engineering triumph for me.

Q: Have you read anything good lately that isn't technical?
A: Yeah, *Surrounded by Idiots*. It's great for understanding why people act the way they do. Also, *How to Build a Car* by Adrian Newey. That one is technically non-fiction, but for me, reading about the engineering triumph in F1 is just pure entertainment.

Q: That blizzard story in the Alps sounds terrifying. Were you scared?
A: At the time, you just go into survival mode. It was a 'snowy night at 3200' meters. We lacked orientation, so we just had to hunker down in a cold bivouac. When the clouds cleared in the morning and I saw the path, the relief was insane. We didn't need the helicopter rescue in the end, but knowing they were there was comforting.

A: I love *StarTrek* and *The Core*. Anything with that mix of engineering triumph, mechanics, and electronics. *RoboCop* is another favorite. I just love seeing machines and humans working together—or against each other!

Q: Did you manage to do any diving on your last trip?
A: Yes! I finally obtained my diving license in Tenerife. I dove at most of the popular spots around Arona and Los Cristianos. It was amazing to finally explore underwater after hiking Teide so many times.

Q: Do you have any big plans for the future?

Q: Are you working on any renovation projects?

A: I'm really getting into Private Agents—running local LLMs on my own hardware. But honestly, the coolest thing is just fixing up my house. I love woodworking. A: Hiking is my main thing. I try to stay active. When we were in Tenerife, I hiked all the way up Teide on foot. It's a killer workout but the view is worth it. I also try to do active sports whenever I can.

A: It was short but nice. We spent 3 days there visiting my cousin and his family while they were on holiday. It’s different from Tenerife—much windier, very sandy. But it was great to see family and relax a bit.
